Definition: from G4862 and G1401; a co-slave, i.e. servitor or ministrant of the same master (human or divine):--fellowservant.
BiblicalUsage: Paul calls Epaphras his dear fellow servant, who learned the gospel for the Colossians and is a faithful minister of Christ, and in the parable the unforgiven servant lays hands on his fellow servant over a hundred pence. A fellow servant is one who serves the same Master, and the parable turns on forgetting it: a man forgiven a fortune will not forgive a pittance from one who serves beside him.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that I serve beside every other servant of the same Master, and I believe a forgiven servant who will not forgive has forgotten whose household he is in.
